sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signals, signs and work zones

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Delaware’s right-of-way laws identify who must yield; yielding to prevent a crash remains appropriate regardless of the assigned duty. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Traffic signs and signals apply to people walking, cycling and driving on streets or highways. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
The red-light camera program photographs violators, records plate numbers and mails citations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
The handbook’s basic signal cue is red for stopping, yellow for preparing to stop and green for cautious progress. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
A signal arrow governs only the direction it points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
At steady red, stop at the line, otherwise before the crosswalk, or before the intersection if neither exists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
A right turn at red requires a complete stop and is allowed only when safe and when neither a sign nor a steady red arrow forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
After a complete stop, a safe left turn on red from one one-way street into another is permitted unless a sign or steady red arrow forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow announces the change from green to red; prepare to stop, but cross cautiously if already too close for a safe stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
A steady green permits safe forward movement or a turn unless another signal or sign prohibits that turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
On green, yield to people and vehicles already in the intersection or neighboring crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
When turning on green, take particular care around pedestrians and opposing traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Treat flashing red like a stop sign: stop completely and move only when safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Flashing yellow calls for reduced speed, heightened attention and cautious movement through the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
When an installed signal shows no illuminated indication, reduce speed and get ready to yield to vehicles in or nearing the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A03
Round signal lenses apply in every direction, while an arrow is direction-specific. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A03
A steady red arrow requires a complete stop and prohibits movement in its direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A03
A flashing red arrow allows a turn in its direction after a complete stop and selection of a safe traffic gap. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A03
A steady yellow arrow ends the green-arrow interval; continue carefully if too close to halt safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A03
A flashing yellow arrow permits the indicated movement after yielding to opposing vehicles and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A03
A steady green arrow permits cautious movement in its direction, with yielding to people and vehicles lawfully occupying the intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A04
Where pedestrian and vehicle signals work together, drivers follow vehicle signals and pedestrians follow WALK or DON’T WALK indications. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A04
WALK permits a pedestrian to proceed while remaining alert for turning vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A04
Drivers must yield to a pedestrian displaying a WALK indication. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A04
A pedestrian already crossing when DON’T WALK begins flashing should finish crossing as quickly as possible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A04
A pedestrian who has not begun crossing must not start during flashing DON’T WALK. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A04
A steady DON’T WALK means a pedestrian must not begin crossing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A05
Accessible pedestrian signals provide nonvisual crossing information through sounds, spoken messages or vibration. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A05
Accessible pedestrian signals communicate when the WALK interval starts and ends to blind or visually impaired people. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A05
Audible pedestrian signals can also guide direction at angled intersections and wide crossings. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A05
Pressing the crosswalk button activates a HAWK sequence that stops traffic for crossing and later resets after traffic resumes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A05
Rectangular rapid-flashing beacons at pedestrian or bicycle crossings are activated by a pedestrian’s or cyclist’s push button. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A05
A rectangular rapid-flashing beacon uses a rapid stuttering flash pattern. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A05
When a rapid-flashing crossing beacon operates, slow down, check for pedestrians and bicyclists, and yield when needed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A06
Circular or arrow signals designated by a bicycle sign govern bicyclists in the specified bicycle lanes or paths. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A06
Bicycle-shaped signal indicators have circular-signal meanings for bicyclists in designated bicycle lanes or paths. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A06
Cyclists riding in general traffic lanes must follow the normal round and arrow signals. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A06
A highway sign’s shape, color, wording and symbols help identify its information. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A06
Regulatory signs communicate laws about such matters as direction, lane use, turns, speed and parking. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A06
Regulatory signs are commonly white, red or black and may be rectangular, square or specially shaped. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A06
The stop sign is the highway’s only eight-sided sign and has white lettering on red. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F42 | anchor: A06
At a stop sign, stop fully at the line; if absent, at the crosswalk; if both are absent, before the intersection. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F43 | anchor: A06
Before leaving a stop sign, yield to vehicles and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, checking for less conspicuous road users. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F44 | anchor: A06
At a yield sign, give way to vehicles and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, stopping if needed, and proceed only when safe. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F45 | anchor: A06
Approach a yield sign slowly, check both directions and yield to lawful movements and crossings. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F46 | anchor: A06
A posted speed-limit sign establishes the limit for that highway segment. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F47 | anchor: A06
International turn-prohibition signs used in Delaware include prohibitions on left turns, right turns and U-turns. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0074]

Misconceptions: Preserve the source’s conditions, exceptions and may-versus-must distinction when recalling a rule.
Mnemonics: Use “cause, condition, consequence” as an authored cue for reviewing each cited rule.
Glossary: The key source terms are retained in the individual facts and their domain labels.
Dynamic facts: Contact details, provider lists and current service availability require fresh confirmation and stay outside the stable fact set.
